situation: I sell handmade leather wallets online. A customer bought one 5 weeks ago (my window is 30 days) and wants a refund because the stitching came loose on one side. $85.
reply: Sorry the stitching came loose on the side, that shouldn't happen at five weeks. It's past the 30-day return window, but loose stitching is a defect, so that one's on me: I'll restitch it or send you a new wallet, whichever you prefer, and I'll cover the postage both ways. Just tell me which and I'll send a prepaid label today.
note: A defect isn't a change of mind, so the window isn't the point. Fix it fast and generously.

situation: Tenho um estúdio de pilates. Uma aluna, a Fernanda, cancelou a aula particular de amanhã às 8h com menos de 24 horas de antecedência e pediu reembolso dos R$ 120. A regra é clara, mas ela é aluna há dois anos.
reply: Oi Fernanda, tudo bem, cancelei a aula de amanhã. Como foi com menos de 24 horas, o valor não é reembolsável, mas não quero que você perca: posso remarcar para qualquer horário até o fim de outubro, sem custo. Quer que eu reserve quinta às 8h?
note: O não vem com uma alternativa concreta logo em seguida, sem linguagem de política.

situation: Customer bought a $240 custom embroidered jacket from my shop, it matches their approved proof exactly, and now says they 'just don't like it' and will dispute the charge if I don't refund.
reply: I'd really rather sort this directly with you than through the bank, and I think we can. Because the jacket was made to the proof you approved on 12 September, I can't refund it in full, since I can't resell it. What I can offer today is a 40% refund, $96, or I'll change the embroidery colour for free if that's what's bothering you. Tell me which works, or what would.
note: Calm, one-line reason, a real partial offer. If they file anyway, send the bank the approved proof and stop negotiating in the thread.
